nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

Built by correcting each of the ten Phase-3 direct-Sun exposures (1102.D-0954(A), 2023-08-02) with ESO Molecfit 4.4.4 against the observation-night La Silla NOAA GDAS column, then re-stacking and renormalising through pipeline.spectra_normalize -- the same functions that built solar_harps. LINEAGE IS PROVEN, NOT A

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1213: the two new near-UV Fe I Reference Gerber-LTE rows landed after the previous annotation pass. Every near-UV product must state the band's residual opacity deficit or it reads as a converged answer.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

products.xi_note: xi APPLIES to this product and the derivative is OWED — this is not an exemption. products.sigma_reported_caveat: INCOMPLETE: no dA/dxi exists for this pool, so the xi term is absent from this bar rather than zero. The bar is a LOWER BOUND.
products.aggregate_collision_note: Published A is the MEDIAN of the per-line abundances (nlte_effect.json: aggregator=median). LTE 7.541 / NLTE 7.562 — the <3D>-NLTE departure is live and separates the pair on this holding.

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1213: the two new near-UV Fe I Reference Gerber-LTE rows landed after the previous annotation pass. Every near-UV product must state the band's residual opacity deficit or it reads as a converged answer.

products.atlas: KPNO 1984 FTS solar flux atlas, molecfit-corrected
products.telluric_state: corrected: ESO molecfit 4.4.4, six registered bands (RYA-940)
products.grade_variant: full laboratory pool — every primary-lab gf line canonical_gf holds in this band, on OUR gf scale, with the depth gate not applied (RYA-1213)
products.line_set_basis: DERIVED at read time from `tier` by pipeline.reference_lineset.line_set_for_product -- not stored as an identity field (RYA-1127). Shown here for readability; the identity key resolves it independently.
products.xi_source: RYA-587 budget stellar.xi: paired xi 0.90/1.10 legs on this product's own pool
products.xi_note: per-line paired differential at xi 0.90/1.10 on this product's OWN pool, stamped legs (RYA-1178 A)
products.sigma_reported_basis: quadrature(sigma_stat, sigma_syst_complete) where sigma_syst_complete = quadrature(published sigma_syst, sigma_xi). sigma_xi enters ONCE, through sigma_syst_complete — the RYA-1120 artifact's own sigma_reported omitted sigma_syst altogether.

science_provenance.atlas_citation: RYA-940 telluric-corrected sibling of solar_kpno; the 1984 atlas itself is UNMODIFIED. Six registered telluric bands corrected per band with ESO molecfit 4.4.4 on Sirius. NO OBSERVATION METADATA EXISTS for this atlas -- no airmass, no date, no site -- so the RYA-380/927 observation-night-GDAS rule is unsatisfiable and the columns are fitted freely against the MIPAS std atmosphere. Ryan ratified th

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

archive.syst_basis: INTERIM LOWER-BOUND FLOOR (RYA-908/1133): the run's own budget totals 0.1095 dex, dominated by a band-flat 0.10 pseudo-continuum term. RYA-1133 measured the two Kitt Peak holdings returning 7.957 vs 7.697 on the SAME 12 lines - 0.260 dex apart, half-spread 0.130 - so the run's term is breached by its own holdings and 0.130 is published instead. A LOWER bound: two realisations are not the space of them, and all three near-UV atlases are Kitt Peak, so the disagreement can be measured but never adjudicated. Pending RYA-1133's per-ion term.

Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and four windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. The four Fe I rows are NOT — publish_product refuses their DEEPGRADED tier because the pool is mixed-gf (one systematic:K07 line among 55 lab lines, RYA-855 rung 1), a refusal that is identical with molecules off and therefore not caused by this change. Their molecular values are measured and recorded in data/results/rya1207/nearuv_molecular_lever.json, pending Ryan's ruling on the tier.

irreducible_dispersion.basis: sigma_stat x sqrt(n_lines); valid because sigma_stat is the STANDARD ERROR of the mean — verified against the per-line layer on the VIS products that carry both (std/sqrt(n) reproduces the published stat_dex; the raw std does not)
irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

Not adopted for the headline. irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

archive.aggregate_collision_note: Published A is the MEDIAN of the per-line abundances (nlte_effect.json: aggregator=median). On this holding the <3D>-LTE and <3D>-NLTE medians coincide at 7.552 while their MEANS differ by +0.0267 dex and the NLTE departure moves 66 of 67 lines. The pair is NOT byte-identical and the NLTE leg is NOT unwired: the same code path on kpno_kurucz2005 gives 7.541 vs 7.562. Genuine median coincidence, kept as two products (RYA-1178 Part 0).

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.

Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.

archive.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
archive.annotation_reason: RYA-1213: the two new near-UV Fe I Reference Gerber-LTE rows landed after the previous annotation pass. Every near-UV product must state the band's residual opacity deficit or it reads as a converged answer.
archive.superseded_reason: RYA-1232: built on the near-UV line list that silently dropped 13,029 zero-vdW lines (Turbospectrum deletes an atomic line with fdamp 0.0). Rerun on the fixed list; its budget HOLDS (more than 5% of the pool leaves across the uncertainty legs), so no corrected value replaces it and the known-biased one is not kept live.

gaps.reason: EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION, measured on all three arms 2026-08-24. Of the 70 Fe I lab lines in 6910-9199 A, ZERO sit above the 0.60 central-depth gate — the harness refuses with 'no graded line in this band sits above the EW depth gate' before any spectrum is read, identically for KP1984-molecfit, KP2005 and IAG. The depth split is a strong function of wavelength: near-UV 58 of 59 deep, VIS 109 of 176, red-optical 0 of 70. Red-optical's GRADED tier therefore IS the whole lab pool. Do not relaunch this as a missing run.

CRIRES+ Y GRADED is n=1 and the harness REFUSES it — measured 2026-08-26, not inferred. Of the 5 primary-lab Fe I lines in the Y arm (9913.180 DH14, 9944.207 DH14, 10142.844 DH14, 10216.313 RU14, 10435.355 DH14) only 10435.355 falls inside the conditioned 10280-10680 A window; the other four sit BELOW 10280, in the stretch Elgueta's window excludes. The harness refusal is correct and quotable: 'a pool of fewer than 2 lines cannot carry a line-to-line scatter, so its statistical term would be invented rather than measured'. Deep-graded is 0 in the same window. ⚠️ This is a WINDOW limit, not an arm limit: the Y arm spans 9796.5-10796.1 A and is telluric-clean below 10280 (0.00-0.26% of points below 0.5, vs 0.06-0.21% INSIDE the adopted window), so a widened conditioned derivative reaches n=5. That derivative exists (vesta_crires_plus_Y_9800_10796_normalized.csv) but is not yet a registered holding.
